title: Go-Bag (Evacuation Bag)
description: Use this list to pack one carry-able bag per person that lasts about 72 hours if you must evacuate on short notice.

sources.title: Anatomy of a First Aid Kit

items.text: At least a 7-day supply of each prescription medicine in labeled containers, plus a written list of medicines, doses, and allergies
Water: 1-2 liters (1-2 quarts) carried per person, plus a filter or purification tablets to treat more
3 days of no-cook food (about 2,000 calories per adult per day): bars, nut butter packets, jerky, crackers, dried fruit
First aid kit: gloves, bandages, gauze, tape, antiseptic wipes, blister care, emergency blanket, and a tourniquet you know how to use
Copies of IDs, insurance cards, and medical records in a waterproof zip bag
Cash in small bills - card readers and ATMs fail without power
Headlamp or flashlight with spare batteries
Phone charging cable and a charged power bank
Battery or hand-crank radio that gets NOAA Weather Radio
Written phone numbers, an out-of-area contact, and a meeting place on a card
Spare glasses or contact lens supplies, hearing aid batteries, and chargers for any medical device
N95 masks for smoke, dust, or illness
Whistle to signal for help
Rain jacket or poncho, warm hat, and a full change of clothes with extra socks
Sturdy walking shoes if you do not wear them every day
Emergency bivy or space blanket and a light tarp
Hygiene kit: hand sanitizer, wet wipes, toilet paper, toothbrush, soap, menstrual supplies, trash bags
Multi-tool, duct tape, 50 feet (15 m) of cord, and work gloves
Two ways to make fire (lighter and waterproof matches) for warmth or boiling water
Printed local map with two evacuation routes marked
Metal cup or small pot, spoon, and a manual can opener if you packed cans
Comfort items and small activities for children; food, leash or carrier, and records for pets
Notebook and pencil
Use a sturdy backpack lined with a trash-compactor bag; keep the full bag light enough to walk with (about 20% of body weight or less)
Store the bag by an exit, not in the attic, and check it every 6 months: food, water, batteries, medicines, and clothing sizes
